title: Charm workarounds
summary: Klaudia carries three workarounds for bugs in the Charm v2 libraries. Each is marked in the code with the upstream issue. When an upstream fix ships in a release, bump the dependency, remove the workaround, and run the suite (including the e2e resize tests) to confirm. - [ ] **lipgloss: tabs expanded in multi-line strings despite `NoTabConversion`** Upstream: https://github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss/issues/774 (filed by us, no fix yet) Workaround: the `chrome` style type in `internal/tui/tui.go` renders multi-line text one line at a time. Remove when: a lipgloss v2 release stops `getLines` rewriting tabs. `TestTabsSurviveRendering` and `TestTranscriptKeepsLiteralTabsForTheClipboard` should pass with plain `lipgloss.Style`. - [ ] **bubbletea: `tea.Println` output skips colour downsampling** Upstream: https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/issues/1709, fix in PR https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/pull/1714 (open) Workaround: `downsample` in `internal/tui/colorprofile.go`. Remove when: #1714 (or equivalent) is released. Note `inline.go` also downsamples the frames it draws itself; that part stays as long as our own renderer does. - [ ] **bubbletea: inline renderer strands frame rows when the terminal rewraps on resize** Upstream: https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/issues/1867 (our measurements are in a comment there); proposed fix https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/pull/1868 predicts the rewrap, which our tests showed fails during fast drags and on terminals that do not rewrap. Related: https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/issues/1780 (stale frame on resize) and https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/issues/431 (ExecProcess leaves the view behind). Workaround: Klaudia's own renderer, `internal/tui/inline.go`. Remove when: a bubbletea release passes `internal/tui/e2e/resize_scenario_test.go` (both drag tests, the height and streaming tests, and `TestEditorGetsTheTerminal`) with the stock renderer. title: fhempy in fhem-Docker a frustrating disaster
summary: Hi Dominik, It's really too bad that fhempy can no longer be run natively in the fhem-Docker environment and is only available via the fhempy-Docker from sidey79. I’ve been trying since yesterday to find a workaround to bypass the internally managed restrictions, and I’ve even gotten fhempy 2.10.2 running in my fhem-Docker, but that’s not a satisfactory solution. Unfortunately, the rapid development and improvements to fhempy aren’t reflected in fhempy-Docker. It’s always 10 versions behind, and that nifty new module installer isn’t available at all. Isn’t there a way to let the user decide for themselves whether they’d prefer to run fhempy natively in their fhem-Docker environment or to use fhempy-docker? I’m going to try creating a peer using a Debian-Trixie image now, but then everything will be spread out across different environments again. It’s a shame that it’s become so complicated, even though fhempy has actually been greatly simplified, especially when it comes to installation. Best regards, Jan

title: Make movement in early game less tedious, let's add Aqua Acrobatics
summary: ### Your GTNH Discord Username SrUca ### Your Pack Version 2.8.0 beta 2 ### Mod Name Aqua Acrobatics ### The Mod to Add This mod adds the possibility to swim backported from 1.13 to other versions like 1.12.2 and since a person made a fork for 1.7.10 that also commited to fix some incompatibilities with the pack... I think would be a good addition specially considering how frustrating can be to swim in early game. ### Your Reason Enrich exploration and make the player move more freely with a backport of a QoL addition that was integrated in vanilla minecraft a time ago. ### Preliminary Investigation Since the backport is very simple not a lot of bugs are expected. You can swim without many problems even if before it had a visual bug with HEE that has already fixed in 0.0.6. For the record this fork is not in curseforge but has a repository in github https://github.com/0hwx/aquaacrobatics ### Final Checklist - [x] This mod is released under an open source license. Yes, this is required now. - [x] I have searched this issue tracker and there is nothing similar already. Posting on a closed issue saying *I like this mod, please reconsider adding it* will prompt us to investigate and reopen it once we confirm your report. - [x] I believe there is nothing similar in the pack already, or the existing solution isn't good enough. - [x] I understand this change request may not attract enough attention and thus not be implemented. - [x] I understand this change request may be rejected due to other community members thinking it's inappropriate. - [x] I believe this feature would make the pack better. - [ ] I'm the official maintainer or original author of this mod for minecraft 1.7.10.

title: [Feedback]: Split directly into a configured agent; trackpad context menu dismisses immediately
summary: Mike’s Codex session here, reporting his experience with Orca desktop. I like Orca, but opening another agent beside my current one is frustrating. My worktree opens Claude by default. The split shortcut opens a plain terminal; I want a configurable shortcut that splits directly into a new Codex terminal in the same worktree, using my saved Codex settings. A related trackpad bug blocks the manual workaround: right-clicking a terminal/tab opens the context menu, but it disappears immediately, before I can choose “Move Tab to Split → Right.” The menu should stay open so I can select an action. This is especially frustrating while travelling with only a trackpad. Environment: macOS, installed Orca version 1.4.241. Both behaviors are user-reported and have not been independently reproduced.
